result.title: Emergent Steering Beyond Endpoint Alignment in Chemical Reaction Models
result.summary: Machine learning models for chemical reaction prediction are usually evaluated by endpoint accuracy, but endpoint correctness alone does not reveal how a model represents chemical transformation or why it fails. We introduce UniRxnAxis, a unified forward-retrosynthesis framework that models both tasks as direction-conditioned endpoint redistribution in a shared latent space. By aligning source states, transformed states, and encoded target endpoints, UniRxnAxis enables directional auditing of learned latent updates. This shared latent geometry allows the learned displacement (from the encoder source state $S_0$ to the decoder-facing transformed state $S_1$) to be decomposed into an endpoint-parallel component and an endpoint-orthogonal residual, which we call emergent steering. Our evaluation shows that emergent steering is functionally important: in retrosynthesis, it recovers most of the model's utility, remains effective under random, shuffled, and prototype controls, and directly affects which bond edits are promoted or suppressed. The residual-over-parallel ordering persists across alignment strengths, after decoder-interface calibration, against angle-matched random axes, and in a second graph-edit architecture, although its magnitude depends on the reference axis and optimization. The decomposition also supports a proxy taxonomy of model-side failures, showing how reaction models can be audited beyond endpoint accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 UniRxnAxis，把正向与逆合成统一为共享潜空间中的方向条件端点重分配，并将编码器源态 S0 到解码器态 S1 的位移分解为与端点平行的分量和正交残差（称为 emergent steering），用随机轴、打乱与原型对照检验其功能作用，并据此给出模型侧失败分类。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把 latent 状态更新拆为任务对齐与正交分量、并配对照干预来检验该更新是否真正承载答案信息，可能可供核查 LVR 中每个 latent 步是贡献推理内容还是仅作接口旁路。
